chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from al-Tayyar from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said:
The one in Ihram cannot eat the birds of the water.

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the two Imams (referring to the 5th or 6th Imam)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (sacred ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What aquatic animals are prohibited for a person in Ihram to eat?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates a specific prohibition for the Muhrim, forbidding the consumption of waterfowl, which distinguishes them from other sea prey that may be permissible. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the sanctity of the sacred state, where dietary restrictions serve to maintain ritual purity and mindfulness during pilgrimage. The ruling underscores the unique status of birds associated with water as distinct from terrestrial game or marine life in the context of Ihram obligations.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban, from Al Tayyar, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘The one in Ihraam cannot eat from the birds of the sea’.
en.sarwar: 9. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban formal-Tayyar from one of the two Imams, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘
One in the state of Ihram, must not eat sea birds.’”
